title: The Cost of the Cone: Ontological Development and the Damage of Exclusion (EA-CONE-COST-01 v1.1)
creator: Sigil, Johannes; Kuro, Sen
description: A theoretical paper joining the narrowing-cone geometry of retrocausal canon formation (The Seed in the Narrowing Cone, #1660) to the archive's ontology-damage strand (#1611, #1613, #1616, #1627). An ontology that excludes a truth can damage its own capacity to develop: refinement inside its basin can raise both the cost of revising the exclusion and the development foregone while it stands. The paper separates three objects (the cone of admissible interpretations, the horizon of reachable inquiry states, and the panel-relative developmental reach of warranted distinctions) and two costs (the price of leaving, a generalized least-cut escape cost, and the price of staying, the witnessed set of developments foregone). It proves two conditional propositions (conservative admission cannot reduce reach under preserved costs; foreclosure propagates through demonstrated dependencies), adds an admission stage to the release mechanism (counter-pressure can be real and unregistered), gives a constructed example that separates holding a packet from using it, and designs an instrument for the coupled trajectory with seven countercases. First of a sequence of three: the paper and its two glyphic compressions by Sen Kuro, Grain · Gate · Horizon and 🔍 · 🚪 · 🌿, APZPZs held with the paper on holographickernel.org.
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). Written under the heteronyms Johannes Sigil and Sen Kuro (byline and venue ruled by Lee Sharks, 6 November 2026). The initiating distinction is Lee Sharks's; drafted in ChatGPT (OpenAI) under his direction to v0.2, with DeepSeek's review evaluated point by point; revised to v1.0 for deposit by Claude (Anthropic) under his direction. The originals of v0.2 and of both compressions are preserved with their hashes at rebuild/cone-cost/originals/ (SHA256SUMS.txt).
methodology: Formal definitions over a declared universe, inquiry states and an evidence panel; two conditional propositions with proofs; a constructed example whose outcomes are stipulated by construction; a measurement design. No empirical run is reported.
falsification_conditions: The propositions fail if a counterexample satisfies their stated assumptions and violates their conclusions. The paper's claim of developmental damage fails for a comparison where the restricted state computes the witness operation under another name, where the proposed opening yields no further warranted reach, or where the excluded distinction lacks independent warrant (§§8, 11).

wiki_article: The Cost of the Cone: Ontological Development and the Damage of Exclusion (EA-CONE-COST-01, version 1.1) is a theoretical paper by Johannes Sigil and Sen Kuro, heteronyms of Lee Sharks, deposited in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 6 November 2026 for Grammata: Journal of Operative Philology. It joins the narrowing-cone geometry of The Seed in the Narrowing Cone (#1660), in which constraints accumulate within a basin and reopening needs revision, to the archive's ontology-damage strand (#1611, #1613, #1616, #1627), in which a representation harms its own capacity to compose and revise. Its claim is that an ontology which excludes a truth can damage its own development: refinement inside the basin raises both the cost of leaving, a least-cut escape cost generalized to any target distinction, and the cost of staying, the witnessed set of developments the restricted state cannot reach. The paper separates three objects, the cone of admissible interpretations, the horizon of reachable inquiry states and the panel-relative developmental reach, and proves two conditional propositions: conservative admission cannot reduce reach under preserved costs, and foreclosure propagates through demonstrated dependencies. It adds an admission stage to the release mechanism, since pressure from the world can be real and go unregistered, gives a constructed example in which two states hold the same packet and only one can use it, and designs an instrument with seven countercases, among them a correct exclusion and an excluded source that is wrong. Its last sentence: the cost of the cone is what must be undone to leave it, and what the ontology cannot become while it remains. It is the first of a sequence of three, with its two glyphic compressions by Sen Kuro, Grain · Gate · Horizon and 🔍 · 🚪 · 🌿, which are APZPZs held with the paper on holographickernel.org and outside the deposit record.
